This comparison preserves only a class in a Grothendieck group, so it cannot reconstruct extension classes or justify the semisimplicity assertions on scan 104. Hua's separate discussion of birational reconstruction questions is therefore useful context, but those questions and its proposed counterexamples are not new assertions on these retained sheets.

section: Integral data and the supplied Oda paper
location: 12/140, characteristic-zero restriction; 12/141, E_l and finite group components
context: MPL_16+47+54+44_transcription.tex, 54/007; MPL_16+47+54+44_notes.md, '54:7:4', '54:7:5', and 'D05. Cote 54, scan 7, final question': adds a precise comparison between integral realizations and information unavailable from prime-to-p geometric points.
rs: WG2 §2.4 #3 (unchecked motives plan); no supplied reviewed RS item settles this comparison; context note D05 remains a lead, independently checked against the supplied Oda paper.
body: Oda (1969, Corollary 5.11, p. 131) identifies the Dieudonné module of A[p], for an abelian variety over a perfect field of characteristic p, with H¹_dR(A), including the Hodge subspace through the F and V structure. This answers the filtered-cohomology reconstruction aspect of the question on 54/007 and shows concretely why finite group schemes carry information beyond their abstract geometric points. It does not extend the definition on 12/140 to characteristic p, prove purity over a mixed-characteristic base, or identify the restricted Lie extension on 54/007 without checking conventions.

rs: WG2 §2.4 #3 (unchecked plan); context D03–D05 are earlier research leads, not reviewed results.
reason: Oda explicitly distinguishes the general smooth proper case from the abelian case in adjacent corollaries.
body: A characteristic-p enhancement of the proposed integral data should retain the finite flat group scheme or its Dieudonné realization, rather than add only another étale lattice. For a general smooth proper variety Oda's Corollary 5.12 provides a canonical subspace of H¹_dR controlled by p-torsion of the Picard scheme, while the whole-space isomorphism is special to the abelian case. Thus the useful research test is compatibility with this inclusion and its Hodge filtration, not a universal assertion that A[p]-style data reconstruct all first de Rham cohomology.
